title: Tilda and the Lost Mouse
markdown:
Whoooo knows what wonders can be found when the world is quiet and the moon is just beginning to peek? Now, gather close, little listeners, and let wise old Owl tell you a tale from the very heart of the Misty Crags. The moon, you see, is like a friendly lantern in the sky, guiding all the little creatures home.

It was a sunny afternoon. The air smelled like flowers and damp earth. Tilda, a young witch with hair like spun moonlight, was gathering nice-smelling leaves near her lovely, cosy cottage. Her cottage was built right into a gentle hill. Its roof was covered with soft moss, and its chimney sent out happy little puffs of smoke that smelled like lavender.

As Tilda hummed a little tune, her basket filling with thyme and mint, she heard a tiny sound. It was like a little whisper. She peeked behind a mossy stone that looked like a sleeping hedgehog. There, shaking on some clover, was the smallest creature she had ever seen. It was a field mouse, no bigger than her thumb. His whiskers twitched like little feelers, and his eyes were like shiny dark beads. This was Squeaky Mittens, and he was very, very lost.

"Oh, dear me," whispered Tilda, her voice as soft as rustling leaves. "You look like you can't find your home, little one. Your whiskers seem to be pointing everywhere!"

Squeaky Mittens wrung his tiny paws together. They looked like two small pebbles. "I can't!" he squeaked, his voice like a tiny bell. "I was chasing a fat, stripey ladybug! A very exciting one! And now… oh dear… I don't know which way is home! My tummy feels fluttery." It was a big problem for such a small mouse.

Tilda's heart felt warm and kind. She knew how important it was to feel safe. "Don't you worry, Squeaky Mittens," she said. Her voice made him feel safe, like a warm blanket. "We'll find your burrow. We'll set off right away, before it gets dark and the path gets hard to see." The thought of him being alone as night came made her feel a little sad, but a good sad because she wanted to help.

And so, with Squeaky Mittens perched on Tilda’s shoulder, his little nose twitching and his tiny claws holding on gently, they began their journey. The path went through tall pine trees. Their needles sighed softly in the dimming light. It sounded like the trees were sharing secrets with the wind. Squeaky Mittens let out little "eep!" sounds when a branch rustled. "It’s just the wind, Squeaky Mittens," Tilda would murmur. "The trees are just singing a gentle song. And look, see how the little ferns are curling up for a nap?" She pointed out a ladybug, its shell a shiny red, climbing a blade of grass.

As the sky turned pink and purple, Tilda saw a flicker of light. It wasn't a star. It came from a funny tower, a little bit wobbly, like it was still waking up. Its windows glowed like little lamps. This was the home of Barnaby Bumble, a wizard known for his many maps. His tower was so full of maps, they spilled out of the windows and curled around the trees.

Tilda and Squeaky Mittens went to the tower. The air smelled like old paper and warm ink. The door creaked open. Out popped Barnaby Bumble himself, a kindly wizard with a long, pale beard and glasses on his nose. He held a tall pile of scrolls that almost fell over.

"Ah, hello there!" Barnaby boomed, his voice friendly and a little bit rolling. "Lost, are we? Or perhaps found? Come in, come in! Though you might have to step over a map or two. I have maps for everything! Maps of the sky, maps of the sea, maps of where old dragons slept!" He gestured, almost dropping his scrolls. He showed a large map with lines and colourful spots. "Is your home marked with a tiny acorn here, near the Waterfall?"

Squeaky Mittens wriggled. "My home has a cosy root at the entrance," he squeaked, his voice a little stronger. "It looks like a little brown eyebrow above the door!"

Barnaby hummed, looking at another map, then another. His glasses slid down his nose. "A root, you say? Hmm, this map shows a root… or was it a bumpy turnip? And this one… is this a very big crumb?" Barnaby was so busy looking at his maps, his head in a whirl of lines and places, he almost tripped on a map of caves.

Tilda, meanwhile, was looking around with her quick, noticing eyes. Barnaby's maps were wonderful, but Tilda saw other things. She saw how the moss grew thickest on the north side of the trees, like a green coat. She watched the fireflies just starting to light up, heading towards flowers still blooming. And she felt the gentle breeze, which usually blew from the west. Barnaby's maps were interesting, but sometimes, Tilda knew, the best directions were written in nature's own easy-to-read book. It was a secret message from the trees and wind.

"Thank you, Barnaby Bumble," Tilda said kindly. "Your maps are very… very full. They tell wonderful stories. But I think," she said, pointing to ferns that sparkled in the moonlight, "that Squeaky Mittens' home is just that way, past the fireflies, near the big, sleepy oak tree." She could see the shape of the oak in the distance.

Barnaby blinked. "Ah yes! The sleepy oak! Of course! It's right here on this map… if I can just find it under this map of clouds that look like sheep." He chuckled, a sound like dry leaves.

With a final wave, Tilda and Squeaky Mittens hurried on. The path ahead was lit by the first stars, like scattered diamonds. And sure enough, there it was! A tiny burrow under the bent roots of a grand old oak. A root knob stuck out, looking like a doormat. Happy mouse voices chirped from inside.

"Mama! Papa!" squeaked Squeaky Mittens. His worry was gone. He tumbled from Tilda's shoulder, a little brown blur, into the warm hug of his family. There were tiny mouse hugs and little mouse kisses.

Tilda smiled. Her heart felt as full and bright as the big moon rising. Helping Squeaky Mittens had been a small adventure. It made the world feel cosier and brighter. And so, dear listeners, even when maps are confusing, remember that a kind heart and noticing the world around you can always help you find your way. Whoooo knew kindness could be such a good guide?
characters: Tilda the young witch, a mouse
